questions.stem: A company wants an alert when its monthly AWS spending exceeds, or is forecast to exceed, an amount it sets. Which service should it use?

options.rationale: Cost Explorer visualizes and forecasts costs; spending alerts are set in AWS Budgets.
Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you build.
AWS Budgets alerts you when actual or forecasted costs cross thresholds you set.
The Cost and Usage Report delivers detailed line-item cost data to Amazon S3; it does not send alerts.

questions.explanation: The clue is an alert at an amount you set, including forecasted spend, which is AWS Budgets. Cost Explorer also forecasts, but it is for analysis, not threshold alerts.

questions.stem: Which service visualizes and analyzes past AWS costs and usage over time with charts and filters?

options.rationale: Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of planned architectures.
Budgets tracks spending against thresholds you set and sends alerts.
Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.
Cost Explorer shows costs and usage over time and can forecast future costs.

questions.explanation: Cost Explorer is for analysis of actual spend; the Pricing Calculator is for estimates.

questions.stem: A company wants to estimate the monthly cost of an architecture before it builds anything on AWS. Which tool should it use?

options.rationale: Pricing Calculator models the cost of AWS services for a planned workload.
Cost Explorer analyzes spending that has already happened.
Budgets tracks spending against thresholds.
The Cost and Usage Report details actual usage and costs.

questions.explanation: Estimate with the Pricing Calculator, track with Budgets, analyze with Cost Explorer.

questions.stem: Which feature of AWS Organizations combines the charges of several accounts into one bill and can provide volume pricing discounts?

options.rationale: SCPs limit permissions in member accounts.
Consolidated billing gives one bill for all accounts and combines usage for volume pricing.
Tags categorize costs but do not combine bills.
IAM Identity Center manages workforce sign-in.

questions.explanation: The management account pays for all member accounts under consolidated billing.

questions.stem: A company wants to see AWS costs broken down by project and by department. What should it do?

options.text: Create a separate IAM user for each project
options.rationale: IAM users do not organize billing data.

options.text: Use a different security group for each department
options.rationale: Security groups control network traffic, not cost reporting.

options.text: Tag resources and activate cost allocation tags
options.rationale: Activated cost allocation tags let you group costs by your own categories, such as project or department.

options.text: Deploy each project in its own AWS Region
options.rationale: Regions are not a way to categorize costs.

questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags appear in Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report once activated.

questions.stem: Which provides the most detailed, line-item data about AWS costs and usage, delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.rationale: Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of planned workloads.
Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations.
The Cost and Usage Report contains the most comprehensive cost and usage data, as line items delivered to an S3 bucket you own.

options.text: The Bills page in the Billing and Cost Management console
options.rationale: The Bills page summarizes monthly charges and holds invoices, but it does not deliver line-item files to S3.

questions.explanation: The clues are 'most detailed, line-item' and 'delivered to S3'. You can then query the report with Amazon Athena or load it into Amazon Quick.

questions.stem: Which service lets a company centrally manage multiple AWS accounts and apply policies to them?

options.rationale: IAM manages identities within an account.
Organizations groups accounts, applies policies and provides consolidated billing.
AWS Config records resource configurations.
Budgets tracks spending.

questions.explanation: Organizations is the basis for multi-account governance and consolidated billing.

questions.stem: Where can a company see its charges for the current month and download its invoices?

options.rationale: Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements, not invoices.

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks
options.rationale: Trusted Advisor cost checks find ways to save, such as idle resources, but do not show bills.
The Health Dashboard shows AWS events that affect your account.

options.text: The AWS Billing and Cost Management console
options.rationale: Its Bills page shows month-to-date charges by service and lets you download invoices.

questions.explanation: Charges and invoices are on the Bills page of the Billing and Cost Management console. AWS Artifact also offers downloads, but they are compliance documents, not bills.

questions.stem: Which TWO tools help a company estimate or forecast its AWS costs? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: License Manager manages software licenses; it does not estimate or forecast AWS costs.
Cost Explorer can forecast future costs from past usage.
Consolidated billing combines accounts' charges into one bill; it does not estimate or forecast costs.
Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a planned workload.
Cost allocation tags group costs by your own categories; they do not predict them.

questions.explanation: Estimate before building with the Pricing Calculator; forecast running workloads with Cost Explorer.

questions.stem: A company on Basic Support has a question about a charge on its AWS bill. How can it get one-on-one help from AWS?

options.text: Upgrade to AWS Business Support+ to open a case
options.rationale: Account and billing support is free for every customer; a paid plan is needed for technical support, not billing questions.

options.text: Post the question publicly on AWS re:Post
options.rationale: re:Post is a public community forum, not a private channel for questions about your own bill.

options.text: Open a billing case in the AWS Support Center
options.rationale: Every customer can open an account and billing support case in the Support Center at no cost.

options.text: Report the charge to the AWS Trust and Safety team
options.rationale: Trust and Safety handles reports of abuse of AWS resources, not billing questions.

questions.explanation: Account and billing support is part of Basic Support, so the company can open a case in the Support Center without upgrading. Paid plans add technical support cases.
